title: Abelian specialization units with independent coefficient and scheme universes
statement: Let $X,Z$ be schemes in universe $t$ [def-pc-scheme], $i:Z\to X$ a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and $V$ an affine object of the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Fix any coefficient universe $u$ and put $w=\max(u,t+1)$. Assume evaluation at $V$ sends every epimorphism of sheaves valued in $\mathrm{Type}(w)$ to a surjection. Assume every point of $V$ specializes to a point of $V\times_X Z$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. For any functor $B$ on abelian sheaves valued in $\mathrm{AddCommGrpCat}(w)$ equipped with an adjunction $B\dashv i_*$ to the actual sectionwise direct image [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], and every abelian sheaf $M$, the unit component $M(V)\to (BM)(V\times_X Z)$ is bijective. No coefficient ring, scalar extension, or completeness hypothesis occurs.

proof.text: Construct sheafification in the coefficient universe on essentially small models, and left Kan extension using essentially small comma categories. Transport the supplied projective evaluation and specialization conditions to the identity affine basis object by splitting a cover using the large-universe Yoneda identity. The quotient is the actual kernel quotient of the closed-fibre global sections map.

Take the fully faithful affine closed-lift adjunction. Its counit has invertible closed base change. Hence its image contains the closed fibre; flat generalization lifting and the specialization condition make it surjective. The representable cover is epi, so projectivity splits it. Adjunction injectivity makes the other composite the identity.

Covers of the closed fibre lift to covers of the lifted object. Split them there by projectivity and descend their sections through full faithfulness. For precomposition by the lift, equality after sheafification descends by separatedness after lifting covers. Local preimages glue over the finite disjoint-union cover, and its splitting gives a global preimage. Thus the sheafification unit on the closed fibre is bijective, including for an empty affine.

Forgetting abelian groups commutes with sheafification. Across the affine basis equivalences the inverse mate of the commuting direct-image square is invertible. Its unit equation identifies the actual affine unit with the preceding bijection composed with restriction along the invertible counit. For weakly etale localization, compute the rotated site mate as the composite of pullback composition isomorphisms. Conjugating adjunctions shows its inverse mate invertible; the mate unit equation transports the affine computation back to V. Compare with the supplied adjunction by unit_leftAdjointUniq_hom_app.

lean.statement:
theorem proEtale_abelian_unit_bijective_of_specialization
    {X Z : Scheme.{t}} (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i]
    (V : X.ProEt) [IsAffine V.left]
    (hweak : ∀ (P Q : Sheaf (ProEt.topology X) (Type (max u (t + 1)))) (φ : P ⟶ Q),
      Epi φ → Function.Surjective (φ.hom.app (op V)))
    (hspec : ∀ x : V.left, ∃ z : ↥(pullback V.hom i),
      Specializes x ((pullback.fst V.hom i) z))
    (B : Sheaf (ProEt.topology X) AddCommGrpCat.{max u (t + 1)} ⥤
      Sheaf (ProEt.topology Z) AddCommGrpCat.{max u (t + 1)})
    (aB : B ⊣ (proEtaleBaseChange i).sheafPushforwardContinuous
      AddCommGrpCat.{max u (t + 1)} (ProEt.topology X) (ProEt.topology Z))
    (M : Sheaf (ProEt.topology X) AddCommGrpCat.{max u (t + 1)}) :
    Function.Bijective ((aB.unit.app M).hom.app (op V))
